name: All the World's a Stage
description: From Greek tragedy and Shakespeare's Globe to opera houses, Swan Lake and Broadway: how plays, operas and dances became the world's great live shows.

checkpoints.name: Greek theatre
checkpoints.note: In Athens, playwrights such as Sophocles wrote tragedies for religious festivals, setting the questions of fate, law and guilt that later drama kept asking. Theatres then spread through the Greek and Roman worlds for centuries.

checkpoints.name: Before the Globe
checkpoints.note: Sanskrit court plays and Japanese Noh show that theatre grew in many places. In England a glover's son named Shakespeare was born in 1564.

checkpoints.name: Shakespeare's London
checkpoints.note: Across a few busy years Shakespeare's company staged tragedies, comedies and romances at the Globe, while kabuki began in Japan. Friends later collected the plays in the First Folio.

checkpoints.name: Opera and ballet
checkpoints.note: Molière's comedies in the 1600s and Mozart's operas in the 1780s led on to Verdi and Wagner, Tchaikovsky's ballets, Ibsen's realistic plays, Chekhov's quiet dramas and Wilde's comedies, which filled the grand theatres of the nineteenth century.

checkpoints.name: The modern stage
checkpoints.note: Stravinsky's riot, Beckett's waiting men, the longest-running murder mystery and big musicals from Paris to Broadway changed what a theatre could be.
